# Tomnitsky Formula: synthetic check

Scripts for the Tomnitsky Formula, V = C / (C + N), with C > 0 and N ≥ 0.

They compare three one-parameter curves: the hyperbola C / (C + N), the exponential exp(−N / C), and the clipped line max(0, 1 − N / C).

**This repository does not confirm the formula.** The series in `results/` were generated by the script from those curves, plus a little noise. No participant took part. Present-moment clarity, integrity of presence, and active processes in the now were not measured in people. A preregistered study with participants has not started.

The article, version 1.0: [10.5281/zenodo.24270975](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24270975).  
Author: Aleksandr Tomnitsky. The text of the article is under CC BY 4.0. The code in this repository is under the MIT license.

## What the synthetic run says

`analysis_h1_h2.py --synthetic` built 80 series on the steps N = 0, 1, 2, 4. For each series, C was fitted on 0, 1, 2, and clarity at N = 4 was predicted. The hyperbola is counted as ahead only when its error is smaller than both alternatives by at least 0.005.

| Source of the series | Hyperbola ahead |
| --- | --- |
| Hyperbola | 30 of 40 |
| Exponential | 2 of 20 |
| Clipped line | 2 of 20 |
| All series | 34 of 80 |

Read this as a check of the script. When the series comes from the hyperbola, the script usually selects the hyperbola. When the series comes from another curve, it usually does not. Ten of the forty hyperbola series still failed the margin, because each step is a single noisy value. That is a property of this plan, not evidence about people.

The raw summary is `results/report.txt`.

## Scripts

`analysis_h1_h2.py`  
Fits C on the lower steps and predicts the higher step. With `--synthetic` it generates the series and writes `results/`. With `--input file.csv` it reads columns `participant_id`, `n`, `v`. If a person has fewer than three different steps, that person is not tested.

`compare_curves.py`  
The plan for a future file of real sessions: one C fitted on one half of the people, error scored on the other half. It is not a result. No such file of participants exists here.

```bash
python3 analysis_h1_h2.py --synthetic
python3 analysis_h1_h2.py --input sessions.csv
```

## What is not in this repository

No data from participants. No copy of other researchers' archives. No statement that an experiment is already running.
